BitterLessons.name: "Bitter Lessons" Workshop
BitterLessons.speaker: William T. "Bill" Freeman — MIT CSAIL
BitterLessons.about: Headline opening talk, "Bitter and non-bitter lessons" — which hard-won computer-vision lessons genuinely held up under scale and compute, and which did not.
BitterLessons.bio: Thomas & Gerd Perkins Professor of EECS at MIT CSAIL; foundational work on Bayesian / learning-based vision, computational photography, and motion magnification.
BitterLessons.note: Field-reflection workshop — Freeman opens; Alyosha Efros ("Sweet Lessons") and Georgia Gkioxari also feature.

VAR.name: Vision-based Assistants in the Real World (VAR)
VAR.speaker: Michael S. Ryoo — Google DeepMind / Stony Brook (opens the session)
VAR.about: Opening talk of the morning session. Per-talk titles are not yet published, but the program now lists individual times.
VAR.bio: Professor at Stony Brook University and researcher at Google DeepMind; works on video understanding, robot learning, and vision-language models.
VAR.note: All six talks are billed as co-equal "keynote" talks; titles are not posted yet.

EgoVis.name: 3rd Joint Egocentric Vision (EgoVis) Workshop
EgoVis.speaker: Lorenzo Torresani — Northeastern University
EgoVis.about: "Where Perception Isn’t Enough: Anticipation, Guidance & Reasoning Over Video" — recognising actions in first-person video isn’t enough; systems must anticipate, guide the user, and reason over video.
EgoVis.bio: Professor & Aoun Chair at Northeastern; former Meta Research Director. Works on multimodal video understanding and wearable "perceptual AI assistants".

T4V.name: 5th Workshop on Transformers for Vision (T4V)
T4V.speaker: Juan Carlos Niebles — Salesforce AI Research / Stanford
T4V.about: Talk topic not published on the official page (six invited slots with times but no titles).
T4V.bio: Senior Research Director at Salesforce AI Research and affiliated with the Stanford Vision & Learning Lab; works on video understanding and visual reasoning.
T4V.note: No formal keynote designated; the talk topic is unconfirmed by the official page.

COGVL.name: CogVL: Cognitive Foundations for Multimodal Models
COGVL.speaker: Trevor Darrell — UC Berkeley / BAIR
COGVL.about: Closing 40-minute keynote on cognitively-inspired frameworks for vision-language models. (No talk title published.)
COGVL.bio: Professor of EECS at UC Berkeley and founding member of the Berkeley AI Research (BAIR) lab; long-standing work in vision-language learning.

VITA.name: 1st Workshop on Vision for Intelligent Task Assistants (VITA)
VITA.speaker: Kristen Grauman — UT Austin / FAIR (co-headline: Gedas Bertasius, UNC)
VITA.about: "Skill++: Learning to Assess and Improve Physical Skills from Video" — using (egocentric) video to gauge how well someone performs a physical activity and give feedback to improve.
VITA.bio: Professor at UT Austin and research scientist at FAIR; a leading figure in egocentric video (Ego4D / Ego-Exo4D) and embodied perception.
VITA.note: All eight talks are co-equal "invited talks"; the headliner is inferred.

CV4Smalls.name: Computer Vision with Small Data (CV4Smalls)
CV4Smalls.speaker: Juan Carlos Niebles — Salesforce AI Research / Stanford (co-keynote: Vasudev Lal, Oracle)
CV4Smalls.about: "Agentic Ambient Intelligence: Perception, Reasoning & Action" — systems that perceive their environment, reason about it, and autonomously take action.
CV4Smalls.bio: Research Director at Salesforce AI Research and co-director of the Stanford Vision & Learning Lab.

ViSCALE.name: 2nd ViSCALE: Test-Time Scaling for Computer Vision
ViSCALE.speaker: Sergey Levine — UC Berkeley (opening slot; no single keynote designated)
ViSCALE.about: Opening invited talk. No talk titles or abstracts are published on the official page.
ViSCALE.bio: Associate professor at UC Berkeley; known for deep reinforcement learning and robotic control.
ViSCALE.note: Six speakers under a "Keynote Speakers" header, all billed as equal invited talks.

ReLearn.name: ReLearn: Rediscovering Intelligence — Can AI Still Learn from Humans?
ReLearn.speaker: Alexei "Alyosha" Efros — UC Berkeley
ReLearn.about: Opening keynote on the workshop’s central question — what human and cognitive insight can still teach AI vision systems.
ReLearn.bio: Professor of EECS at UC Berkeley (formerly CMU); works at the intersection of computer vision and graphics.
ReLearn.note: Closing keynote by William T. Freeman (MIT).

DataMFM.name: Emerging Directions in Data for Multimodal Foundation Models (DataMFM)
DataMFM.speaker: No keynote designated
DataMFM.about: Four equally-billed invited talks (Ranjay Krishna, Ziwei Liu, Aishwarya Agrawal, Yilun Du).

CVinW.name: 5th Workshop on Computer Vision in the Wild (CVinW)
CVinW.speaker: Mohit Bansal — UNC Chapel Hill
CVinW.about: "Memory, Action, and Skill Planning for Multimodal Agents" — memory, action, and planning capabilities for multimodal AI agents.
CVinW.bio: Professor at UNC Chapel Hill and director of the MURGe-Lab; prominent in multimodal / vision-language learning and grounding.
CVinW.note: 2026 theme: multimodal agents with verbal, spatial & temporal intelligence.

KnowledgeMR.name: 2nd Workshop on Knowledge-Intensive Multimodal Reasoning (KnowledgeMR)
KnowledgeMR.speaker: Paul Liang — MIT
KnowledgeMR.about: "Self-Evolving Multimodal AI" — multimodal systems that adapt and improve themselves over time across modalities.
KnowledgeMR.bio: Faculty at MIT (Media Lab / EECS); foundational work on multimodal and multisensory machine learning.

MAR.name: 6th Multimodal Algorithmic Reasoning Workshop (MAR)
MAR.speaker: Melanie Mitchell — Santa Fe Institute
MAR.about: "Six Principles for Evaluating Cognitive Capabilities in AI Models" — a framework for rigorously assessing reasoning and understanding rather than surface-level performance.
MAR.bio: Professor at the Santa Fe Institute; known for work on analogy, abstraction and AI evaluation, and author of "Artificial Intelligence: A Guide for Thinking Humans".

A2A-MML.name: Workshop on Any-to-Any Multimodal Learning (A2A-MML)
A2A-MML.speaker: Mohit Bansal — UNC Chapel Hill (co-headline: Saining Xie, NYU)
A2A-MML.about: "Multimodal Unification, Communication & Composable Generalization" — unifying modalities into shared models and enabling composable generalization across them.
A2A-MML.bio: Bansal: professor at UNC Chapel Hill (multimodal NLP / vision-language). Saining Xie (NYU): ConvNeXt, Diffusion Transformers (DiT) and Cambrian MLLMs.

LOVEU.name: LOVEU: Long-form Video Understanding
LOVEU.speaker: No keynote designated
LOVEU.about: Five equally-billed invited talks (Yu-Xiong Wang, Manling Li, Yaoyao Liu, Ruben Villegas, Xin Eric Wang).

MMR.name: Multimodal Reasoning (MMR) — page unconfirmed
MMR.speaker: Kristen Grauman / Ranjay Krishna (per my notes)
MMR.about: Grounding video / multimodal reasoning in visual evidence. I could not confirm a single official "MMR" page — the lineup appears to mix talks from GRAIL-V and others.
MMR.bio: Grauman: UT Austin / FAIR (egocentric video). Krishna: Univ. of Washington (Visual Genome, grounding).
MMR.note: No official page matched — link goes to the CVPR 2026 workshop list. Closest real page: GRAIL-V (grailworkshops.github.io).

SAUAFG.name: 2nd SAUAFG: Skilled Activity Understanding, Assessment & Feedback Generation
SAUAFG.speaker: Walterio Mayol-Cuevas — University of Bristol / Amazon
SAUAFG.about: "Skill Evolution" — how human/AI skill develops and is understood over time from video.
SAUAFG.bio: Professor of Robotics, Computer Vision & Mobile Systems at the University of Bristol and an Amazon Scholar; works on wearable / egocentric computing.
